item.title: Valley Vista girls basketball gets consolation in Thanksgiving tournament
item.description: Valley Vista, the defending state 6A girls high school basketball champions, hosted its first Thanksgiving girls basketball tournament on Nov. 23-24 at Surprise. The Monsoon took home a consolation prize in the eight-team annual event. Miami took first place, improving to 5-0 on the young season after sweeping four tournament games, winning three of those games by double-digit margins, including a win over Copper Canyon in the title game. Valley Vista defeated Copper Canyon, 49-42, and Ironwood, 34-31, on Monday. Valley trailed Ironwood for three quarters but scored 13 points in the fourth to pull out a victory. The Monsoon are in their first season under new coach MJ Walker. However, Tuesday was not the same story. Valley lost to Copper Canyon in a Round 2 rematch, knocking it out of championship contention. The Monsoon then played Sunrise Mountain in the third-place game and won, 53-51. Freshman Anasophia Rintoul was the star player for Valley Vista, swishing 3-pointers and dishing out assists both days. Senior Braylin Shaw, a returning member from last season's 6A title team, and freshman Mikayla Voll made their presence known, Voll particularly impressive on the boards. Rintoul averaged of 12 points, four rebounds, and four assists in the tournament. Shaw averaged 13 points. Quotes "We just had to work together more, and talk to each other" - Valley Vista's Anasophia Rintoul "Making sure we are actually learning from our mistakes" - Monsoon head coach MJ Walker, on his mindset after Tuesday's final game. item.title: Smallest school, biggest roar: Redding Christian wins best fan section
item.description: Redding Christian School might have the smallest student population in the Redding area with 150 students at the high school level, but one thing is for certain: Lions fans always show up. In a poll against eight other local high schools , some with over 1,000 students, Redding Christian came through with 2,787 votes (39.9%) to claim the Record Searchlight’s 2026 best fan section honor. “It’s a special atmosphere; it’s one of the best around,” Lions football coach and athletic director Gerald Piper said. “They’re loud, they’re supportive and we couldn’t ask for anything better from our fans.” Volunteer Field at Redding Christian’s Palo Cedro campus is unlike most other high school fields in the area. There’s not a lot of seating available in the bleachers, so to compensate, many fans bring their own seating arrangements and line up along the track next to the field to watch the football team compete on Friday nights. More: High school football | Northern Section championship previews, predictions Some VIPs even drive their vehicles onto the track and set up mini watch parties during games. “I think we have a really cool atmosphere, and a lot of it is the way we’re able to sit along the track here and get really close to the field,” Piper said. It creates a more intimate vibe on Friday nights. Fans who show up early enough to get a seat near midfield can sometimes hear discussions between players and coaches throughout the game, that is when the crowd isn’t too loud. “We don’t have a huge student section, but all the fans come out and support us even when the games aren’t super close and not super entertaining,” senior quarterback Wyatt Shaw said. “The fans still come out and enjoy watching and really cheer us on.” The Lions haven’t given their fans many close games. In nine games played throughout the 2026 season, Redding Christian has outscored opponents 477-53. Regardless, they give their fans a show. The Lions haven't lost on their home field since Sept. 13, 2024. When the football team traveled down to Southern California last year for the 2025 CIF Division 7-AA state championship game — over 500 miles away from home — the Redding Christian fans traveled to support their team. “I was shocked last year when I looked up in our stands and saw how many people made the trip and came down,” Piper said. “Middle schoolers, high schoolers, parents; I thought we’d bring a few, but not as many as we did, so that was awesome.” The Lions made the trip worth it as they claimed their first CIF state title in program history . Yet, the fans show up to more than just football games. Over the past year, Redding Christian has had multiple teams across various sports compete in championship games. Both the boys and girls basketball teams won Northern Section titles during the 2025-26 season, and they both made it to the NorCal regional championship game. item.title: Jets Watch: Stuart Skinner Has Given Scott Arniel a Reason to Rethink His Plans
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Winnipeg Jets begin a three-game road trip Wednesday against the Boston Bruins before visiting the New York Islanders on Friday and the New Jersey Devils on Saturday. The Jets have gone 8-1-1 over their past 10 games, but they’re still sixth in the Central Division despite their impressive turnaround. Playing three road games in four days will force Scott Arniel to make some decisions about how he divides the workload between Stuart Skinner and Nico Daws. After watching Skinner’s performance against the Utah Mammoth on Monday, I’d be tempted to give him a little more responsibility over the next few days. The Jets might have an opportunity to get their No. 1 goalie on a roll at a time when they desperately need to make up ground in the Central Division. The Jets Should Give Skinner a Chance to Build Momentum Skinner stopped 34 of the 36 shots he faced against Utah on Monday, including 25 consecutive shots after allowing two goals in the first period. The Jets were outshot 25-7 over the final 40 minutes, and Skinner deserves a ton of credit for getting them out of that game with two points. The biggest thing I’ve wanted to see from Skinner since he arrived in Winnipeg is consistency. We know he’s capable of stealing games, but we’ve also seen stretches throughout his career where he’s struggled to put together a string of good performances. When he plays as well as he did Monday, I want to see the Jets get him right back in the net and give him a chance to carry that confidence into his next start. I’d give him the start against Boston and, if he plays well, go back to him Friday against the Islanders before turning to Daws against New Jersey on Saturday. There’s value in keeping both goalies involved, but I’d much rather see the Jets come out of this road trip with a confident No. 1 goalie than worry about distributing starts evenly. The Jets have spent much of November digging themselves out of an early-season hole. If Skinner can start playing consistently well behind a team that’s finally finding its footing, Winnipeg could make up quite a bit of ground over the next month. Winnipeg Needs More From Its Second Line As much as I’ve enjoyed watching the Jets’ young forwards develop this season, their second line has gone quiet offensively. item.title: Panthers Have Been Good. Now, Barkov & Marchand Return
item.description: FORT LAUDERDALE — There have been a lot of big trades in the NHL over the past few weeks but Paul Maurice says the Florida Panthers are making a big deal of their own with captain Sasha Barkov poised to join the lineup tonight. “Big trades around the league,’’ Maurice said, “and I think we made the biggest one. We get Barkov for nothing. Great deal.” Throw the return of Brad Marchand into the mix perhaps tonight against Ottawa as well and the Panthers are looking pretty, pretty good. ”Last year, he was our leading scorer,’’ Maurice said, referencing Marchand’s numbers before he was pulled in March. “He almost gets forgotten, but our offensive numbers are under where we would like them to be without him there.’’ The Panthers certainly have not set the NHL on fire through their first 24 games, but they have more than held their own. Florida comes into tonight’s game against the Senators holding the final wild-card spot in the Eastern Conference and sit three points back from the Canadiens — who just traded for Dylan Larkin — for third in the Atlantic Division. A win against Ottawa tonight would give Florida its third straight divisional win after a 0-4 start. ”I thought we have done a good job to this point in the season,” said Brady Tkachuk , who faces the Senators for the second time since his blockbuster summer trade to the Panthers. “With everyone, there is room to grow, always room to get better. But it has just been a blast to be here with this group, learning from so many guys, the coaches, the staff, everyone. I’m having a time right now.” The Panthers, certainly, will be getting a boost with the return of Barkov and Marchand. Although Maurice would not commit to Barkov and/or Marchand rejoining the lineup tonight, he has been hinting at it for the past couple of days. The Panthers have also cleared the salary cap path for Barkov’s return off LTIR first by placing Cole Reinhardt on waivers Sunday — with the second cap shoe dropping Tuesday with Cole Schwindt waived. Barkov missed all of last season with a right knee injury, then hurt his left one in his second game back on Oct. 1 in San Jose. Marchand was shut down at the end of last season, needed surgery in August, but made a quick return to the lineup only to hurt his left knee in the middle of his second game back. The Panthers are happy to have them back — and would love to see them stick around a little longer this time around. “There’s an excitement for me and it is long-term for them as well,’’ Maurice said. “What we look like (Wednesday) night, it won’t be a switch that you can flip back. You miss that much hockey … but (Barkov) is one of the best players in the world. We just haven’t had him here for a year and a half.” Said Tkachuk: “It gives us such a boost. It feels like they haven’t missed a beat out there.’’ ON DECK: GAME No. 25 OTTAWA SENATORS at FLORIDA PANTHERS When: Wednesday, 7 p.m. Where: Amerant Bank Arena, Sunrise Local TV: Scripps Sports — WSFL 39 (Miami/FTL); WHDT 9

item.title: Ivan Toney: Newcastle United make surprise decision on Man United target’s possible return
item.description: Ivan Toney: Newcastle United make surprise decision on Man United target’s possible return Manchester United are looking for a solution to their striker woes in January, and former Brentford striker Ivan Toney is reportedly on their agenda. The Red Devils have failed to score in five of their 11 games in the Premier League this season and have managed just one win in the league. The English giants, who finished third last campaign, are 19th in the table at the moment, and new manager Mauricio Pochettino is staring ahead at a huge challenge. With United striker Benjamin Sesko sidelined for a while and Joshua Zirkzee failing to strike a chord, the Argentine manager will be keen to fix United’s goalscoring woes in January. A recent report relayed by The Peoples Person suggests that they have been offered the chance to sign Toney at the turn of the year. United eyeing Ivan Toney Toney rose through the ranks at Northampton Town before moving to Newcastle United in 2015. He failed to cement a place in the starting XI at St. James’ Park, spending much of his time away on loan. The Englishman eventually joined Peterborough United in 2018, before joining Brentford in the summer of 2020. It was at the Brentford Community Stadium that Toney earned the reputation of a proven marksman, scoring 72 goals and setting up 23 more in 141 appearances. However, the 30-year-old made a surprise decision to move to Al Ahli in the summer of 2024, when he was also linked with a move to Old Trafford. This season, Toney has scored 16 goals and registered four assists in 17 games for the Saudi Pro League side. His efforts have already convinced United to consider a move, but it now appears that the Red Devils will face stiff competition in the race to sign the Englishman. item.title: 76ers Have A Frontcourt Problem: 4 Centers They Could Target Before The Trade Deadline
item.description: Nov 23, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) reacts after a play against the Portland Trail Blazers during the third quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Philadelphia 76ers underwent a massive transformation this offseason. By pairing their pre-existing core of Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey with the likes of Jaylen Brown and LeBron James , the 76ers formed a superteam capable of contending for the title. Sadly, like every NBA team, Philadelphia is facing some hardships . With a 14-4 record, the Philadelphia 76ers remain at the top of the Eastern Conference leaderboard. Even so, their latest 128-111 loss against the Portland Trail Blazers revealed a critical weakness in the current lineup: the lack of big man depth. While Embiid serves as the starting center, the 76ers’ big man depth suffered a significant blow when Ariel Hukporti sustained an injury . Although Jabari Walker and Adem Bona have stepped up in his absence, the sheer lack of size was made brutally evident in the loss to the Blazers . As things stand, Philadelphia remains an elite team with enough potential to be a contender. Still, given what it will take to actually win a championship, the franchise must upgrade their big man depth ahead of the trade deadline. To facilitate this, here are four options that the 76ers could consider moving for: Jalen Smith Proposed Trade Details Philadelphia 76ers Receive: Jalen Smith Chicago Bulls Receive: Dean Wade, 2029 second-round pick As the Philadelphia 76ers look to strengthen their big man depth, one name that should be at the top of their list of targets is Chicago Bulls big man Jalen Smith . Rumors indicate that Smith was on Philadelphia’s radar in the past . Given the state they are in, the 76ers would see value in renewing this interest. Jalen Smith has positioned himself as an extremely versatile player. Although he is marginally undersized for a center at 6’8″, the 26-year-old possesses remarkable athleticism and rebounding ability. When additionally factoring in his floor-spacing upside, he has the tools to be an invaluable asset. item.title: Lincoln sack head coach duo Cohen and Shaw
item.description: Chris Cohen (left) and Tom Shaw had been on the coaching staff together at Lincoln for a number of years before they got the top job together [Shutterstock] Lincoln City have sacked their head coaches Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw just six months after they took joint charge of the Championship side. The pair departed a little over 12 hours after they oversaw a 4-0 defeat at fellow strugglers Charlton Athletic on Tuesday. The loss leaves the Imps just three points above the relegation places in what is the club's first season back in the second tier for 65 years. Cohen and Shaw were assistant coaches under Michael Skubala when Lincoln were promoted as League One title winners last season. They were surprisingly promoted to replace their boss as a managerial double act. Charlton brush aside outclassed Lincoln What next for Lincoln City after coach duo exit? The duo oversaw just four wins from 17 league games this season, and Tuesday's loss at The Valley was their fifth in succession and heaviest since being thumped 6-0 by West Ham in mid-October. Lincoln's chairman Ron Fowler, the American billionaire who took a controlling stake in the club when they were on their way to promotion last season, said the decision to sack the pair was in the "best interests" of the Imps. "We have worked incredibly hard to reach the Championship and will do everything in our power to retain our status in this division," he told the club website. First-team coach Shaun Pearson will take charge of Lincoln, with the support of Paul McShane and David Preece, on an interim basis. Lincoln are next in action on Saturday when they host high-flying Wolves. When Cohen and Shaw got the job at Sincil Bank it came somewhat as a shock because managing football teams in tandem is somewhat of a curiosity in the game. Liverpool famously did with Gerard Houllier and Roy Evans in 1998 when the partnership lasted six months as results slumped, while Tottenham gave it a go with Doug Livermore and Ray Clemence earlier that same decade. The hope was that the Cohen-Shaw show would be a lot more like Coventry's success story under John Sillett and George Curtis, who guided the Sky Blues to FA Cup glory in 1987. Lincoln's decision-makers were proactive in talking up their decision, with sporting director Jez George explaining in June that the appointment "wasn't a case of do the easy thing, but it was absolutely the right thing for the club". Shaw and Cohen were also quizzed at length about how the joint role would work, starting with "who's going to make the subs?" Cohen was upfront when he said "from the outside looking in, it's not normal", but the former Nottingham Forest and West Ham midfielder insisted that the job share was "really normal" to them. How peculiar it might have looked, or how the dynamics between the pair worked, all become somewhat irrelevant in recent weeks as Lincoln's dire run of form has plunged them towards the relegation places. item.description: Liverpool stole incredible transfer from Manchester United Rio Ngumoha Set for New Liverpool Deal as Manchester United Miss Haunts Old Trafford There is a particular cruelty in football when a club lets a gifted young player walk away, then has to watch him flourish at a rival. That sting feels sharper still when the boy in question grew up with your badge in his heart. Rio Ngumoha is moving towards a new Liverpool contract, a significant moment for one of the most exciting young attackers in the country and a reminder of how badly Manchester United misjudged the situation when they had the chance to make him their own. Liverpool moved decisively, offered a pathway, and now look ready to secure the future of a talent who has already started to make a serious impression at senior level. Ngumoha arrived at Anfield from Chelsea in 2024 and his development since then has given Liverpool every reason to act quickly. The club see him as part of what comes next, and it is easy to understand why. He brings pace, fearlessness and that unnerving ability to make defenders backpedal. Young forwards can often flatter briefly before fading into the background, but there is an edge to Ngumoha that suggests something more durable. Manchester United Regret Over Rio Ngumoha The detail that sharpens this story is the one that will irritate United supporters most. Nicky Butt has already revealed that Ngumoha and his family are big Manchester United supporters, and that the player visited the club in his early teens before eventually choosing Liverpool. For United, that should have been the simplest of wins, a talented youngster with an emotional connection already in place, standing in the building and waiting to be convinced. Instead, they let the opportunity drift. In modern football, elite academies are judged not only by facilities and history, but by clarity, conviction and the people delivering the message. United had the advantage of affection and still could not close the deal. Liverpool had no such sentimental leverage, yet they won him over all the same. That tells its own story. Liverpool Contract Plans Show Faith in Anfield Future Liverpool now appear close to rewarding that promise with a fresh and improved deal, a move that would underline just how highly Ngumoha is rated behind the scenes. Bayern Munich are reported to have shown interest amid their own issues in attacking areas, which only adds urgency to Liverpool’s position. Clubs across Europe monitor this level of talent closely, especially when the ceiling looks as high as it does here. Anfield, though, has become the place where his future makes sense. He is not being stockpiled, and he is not being hidden. He is being developed with purpose. That matters to gifted young footballers and to the people advising them. Ngumoha Emerges as Serious Liverpool Option His recent display in Liverpool’s 4-0 win over Manchester United only strengthened the sense that he is ready for greater responsibility.

item.title: NFL fans react to Aaron Rodgers’ potential final pass after Steelers bench four-time MVP
item.description: Photo by Jeff Dean/Getty Images NFL fans are wondering whether Aaron Rodgers has already thrown his final pass in the league after the Pittsburgh Steelers decided to bench the four-time MVP on Tuesday. Rodgers’ last throw in Sunday’s defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles was a touchdown to rookie Max Hurleman. Rodgers found Hurleman on third-and-10 from the 20-yard line, as the rookie caught his first NFL touchdown on his debut. The score cut Philadelphia’s lead to 19-15 with just over a minute remaining, and Pittsburgh converted the extra point. However, the Steelers still lost 19-16 despite Joe Milton playing quarterback for the Eagles. Warren Sharp shared a clip of the play on social media, asking: “Is this the final pass of Aaron Rodgers’ career?” NFL fans were quick to respond, and one joked: “Passing the torch to the first Steeler with the number 84 retired.” Hurleman wears the same number that became famous in Pittsburgh thanks to Antonio Brown. Another fan wrote: “Max Hurleman is going to be a trivia answer in a few years. Good for him.” Others were more sentimental about the possibility of Rodgers calling time on his career : “At least it was a touchdown pass.” Another added: “Would be fitting.” One supporter even suggested Rodgers might have been spared a much worse ending. He posted: “Better than a pick-six in the playoffs against Houston.” At 42, Rodgers is approaching the end of his career, and there are only seven games left in what is expected to be his final NFL season. The Steelers’ decision does not necessarily mean he has played his last snap, but if he does not return, a touchdown pass would be a pretty fitting way to bow out. item.title: Lawson Apologized to Perez to Save His F1 Career After Shocking Death Threats in 2024
item.description: Liam Lawson says he didn’t want to apologize to Sergio Perez for his middle-finger gesture at the 2024 Mexico City GP, but he was told to for the sake of his F1 career, after he and his family received death threats from fans. Both Lawson and Perez were fighting for their respective F1 careers back in the 2024 F1 season. The Kiwi replaced Daniel Ricciardo at Visa Cash App RB, while the Mexican was trying to live up to Red Bull’s expectations. Perez was knocked out of Q1 again and received a penalty for a false start in a dismal run in his home Grand Prix in Mexico. To make matters worse, he came across Lawson in a bid to regain lost places, but the two had a heated exchange. Lawson was seemingly aggressive in his defense, which cost Perez. The Mexican suffered further damage when the Kiwi continued on. The Racing Bulls driver met the Red Bull again later in the race, when he showed his middle finger to him. Fighting for F1 Seat, Career Liam Lawson and Sergio Perez at the 2024 Mexico City GP. Image Credit: Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images via Red Bull Content Pool Speaking on the Great Company with Jamie Laing podcast , Lawson revealed that Perez brake-checked him later in the race, which irritated him. Asked by the hosts about putting his finger up at someone on track, he said: “I didn’t swear at him. Yeah, I pulled the finger at him. That didn’t go down well either. “Yeah, these are the moments again that have, really, I’ve learned from over the years, like it was like my second race in Formula One. I was racing for, basically, I was in VCARB, which is the team I’m in now. I knew that I was in contention for the Red Bull seat at the end of the year, and I knew that the guy who was in it was under pressure. “It was basically that I had a shot at getting a seat. So naturally, it’s like there’s a bit more competition with him, and we’re racing. Unfortunately, it was in his home country, Mexico, and I had a close fight with him,” said Lawson, who explained the whole sequence that led him to show the middle finger. The world feed televised the middle finger moment, but skipped what Perez had done to him in the lead-up to it. Lawson admits it wasn’t the smartest thing to do. But the aftermath was a shock to him and his system, especially on social media. Lawson Was Shocked by the Amount of Death Threats Liam Lawson in the Racing Bulls garage at the 2026 Mexico City GP. Image Credit: Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images via Red Bull Content Pool It was not just him, but his family and friends, whose social media was flooded with horrific messages relating to death threats, etc. “It wasn’t a very smart thing; I know it wasn’t a smart thing to do,” said Lawson on the podcast. “I remember coming in afterwards, the second race in Formula One, and I just also don’t know how big Formula One is at this point. Like, I don’t know. I opened my phone; I’m in Mexico. I haven’t even muted Instagram notifications at this point, and I opened my phone at the end of the race, bro

item.title: Real Madrid president Florentino Perez and Barcelona end Negreira conciliation hearing without agreement
item.description: Real Madrid president Florentino Perez and Barcelona end Negreira conciliation hearing without agreement Real Madrid president Florentino Perez and FC Barcelona and have failed to reach an agreement during a court conciliation hearing in Madrid over the former’s comments on the Negreira case. The meeting, held on Wednesday, November 25, ended without a resolution, leaving Barcelona to consider whether to pursue further legal action against the Madrid president. According to Spanish news agency EFE , the hearing was part of the preliminary process before Barcelona could bring a possible criminal complaint over alleged calumny. The dispute comes from comments Perez made in May , when he accused Barcelona of corruption and questioned whether the club had benefited from favourable refereeing decisions. Barcelona sought a retraction from Florentino Pérez Barcelona initiated the conciliation procedure after Perez’s remarks about the Negreira case. The Catalan club wanted the Real Madrid president to retract the accusations or provide specific details about the referees, matches and decisions he believed had benefited Barcelona. Florentino Perez has refused to reconcile and retract his statements. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Perez had referred to alleged corruption, accused Barcelona of “enriching the referees” and used the expression “Negreira Boys” when discussing officials connected to the period under investigation. Barcelona consider those statements damaging to its reputation and has sought a formal clarification. Conciliation hearing ends without an agreement The hearing took place at the Madrid courts and reportedly lasted around ten minutes. Representatives for both sides left without reaching a settlement, while their lawyers declined to provide further details to the media. EFE reported that legal sources confirmed there had been no conciliation and the failure to reach an agreement means Barcelona can now decide whether to continue with the legal process it began in June. What will Barcelona do next? (Photo by JAVIER SORIANO/AFP via Getty Images) It is crucial to note that the conciliation hearing was not a trial and did not establish whether Perez’s statements were defamatory or whether any criminal offence had been committed. Rather, it was an opportunity for the parties to resolve the dispute before possible further proceedings. So what happens now? Barcelona’s next step will be the central question following Wednesday’s hearing. The club can consider filing a criminal complaint over alleged calumny, although no such complaint had been confirmed as filed at the time of the reports. Legally, Barcelona have up to a year to decide whether to pursue the matter through the courts.

item.title: Barcelona teenage forward set for first senior squad call-up for Champions League clash vs Sabah
item.description: Barcelona teenage forward set for first senior squad call-up for Champions League clash vs Sabah According to SPORT , Oscar Gistau is set to receive his first official call-up to Barcelona’s senior squad after Hansi Flick decided to include the young striker for tonight’s UEFA Champions League meeting with Sabah FK. The 18-year-old was already a notable presence at Barcelona’s final training session in Baku on Tuesday, having been invited to work alongside the first team. Flick adds another attacking option Now, as per the report, that opportunity will extend to him being included in the matchday squad for the fifth round of the league phase of the 2026/27 Champions League. Gistau’s inclusion will give manager Hansi Flick an additional option from the bench. Set to be in the squad vs Sabah. (Photo by Alex Livesey/Getty Images) The youngster was also in Baku with Barça’s Juvenil A squad for their UEFA Youth League match against Sabah U19. Now he gets a chance to experience a Champions League match with the senior setup. Barcelona had named only 22 players initially, leaving room for one more addition under UEFA’s 23-player matchday squad limit. The Catalans are without Lamine Yamal for the game, while Xavi Espart, Rodri, Andreas Christensen and Roony Bardghji are also unavailable. Flick’s decision follows a similar approach during Barcelona’s previous European away trip to Istanbul to face Galatasary. On that occasion, Shane Kluivert was invited to train with the senior squad after travelling with the club’s youth team for their UEFA Youth League fixture. A special moment incoming for Gistau? (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) A highly-rated prospect Gistau is regarded as one of the most promising natural number nines to have emerged from La Masia in recent years. The 18-year-old striker’s development has not been entirely straightforward, with injuries disrupting his progress over the past few seasons. He has begun to find greater continuity this campaign, playing for Juliano Belletti’s Barça Atletic as well as Albert Peris’ Juvenil A side in the Youth League. The opportunity to join Barcelona’s senior squad represents another encouraging step, particularly after the setbacks he has experienced. If the inclusion is confirmed, it will be Gistau’s first official call-up to the Barcelona first team, and could mark the beginning of a significant new chapter in his progression from La Masia .

item.title: Jets at Dolphins: 5 storylines to watch for ahead of Week 12
item.description: The New York Jets and Miami Dolphins will continue their 2026 NFL regular season schedules on Sunday when the two teams do battle at Hard Rock Stadium. Kickoff is slated for 1 p.m. Like there will be every week, there are plenty of expected headlines that will pop up during the days leading up to this one between the Jets (3-8) and Dolphins (1-9). Yes, some will be obvious... but others not so much. With that, here are Jets Wire's five storylines to watch for ahead of Week 12 : Hunt for revenge This is the first time in 2026 the Jets will face an AFC East opponent for the second time. It's always tough to win in your division in the NFL and even tougher to sweep your rival... that's what the Dolphins will be looking to do and New York will be asked about getting their revenge. The Jets are the only team the Dolphins beat so far this year. It was an embarrassing loss at home and Gang Green should be motivated to right that wrong on Sunday. 2027 NFL Draft watch Despite the players both locker rooms wanting a win, that's not what this game is going to be about for onlookers. Once again, the Jets are facing a team that will be in the discussion for a top pick at the 2027 NFL Draft. That was the same scenario we saw last week against the LA Chargers and it's going to remain this week. Many will consider a victory on the field a loss for the draft. Frank Reich's view The Jets offense did not face the best opposition last week in the Chargers, but the offense looked better and New York won the game. That outing was also the first one this season that offensive coordinator Frank Reich was calling plays from the sideline. Will he do that again in Miami? The Jets' play calling from Reich saw a bigger commitment to the rushing attack against the Chargers as opposed to prior games. If Reich is on the sideline again, that could be the case again. Bailey grabbing attention Week by week, David Bailey keeps getting more and more attention from the NFL World. The No. 2 overall selection by the Jets at this year's draft is up to 9.5 sacks this season. Bailey became the first NFL player since sacks were officially tracked in 1982 to record at least 9.5 sacks and six forced fumbles through his first 10 career games. What's in store next for Bailey? Playing for AG? For weeks, it looked like the Jets' locker room had checked out on head coach Aaron Glenn. Were the players motivated by his message anymore? It was a fair question at the time. That all changed last week. It very much looked like the players were locked in. What will the motivation level look like for Glenn in Miami? His future could very much be dependent on that. item.title: Quinton Fortune: Championship is ‘relentless’ for Bolton Wanderers
item.description: Quinton Fortune has enjoyed a fascinating career, playing for European giants Man Utd and Atletico Madrid while also plying his trade for the likes of Bolton and Doncaster Rovers. After leaving Man Utd in 2006 as a Premier League winner, Bolton came calling where Fortune enjoyed a short stint in the top flight under Sam Allardyce. And now Fortune has reflected on his experience in England, as well as his coaching stint at Reading between 2020 and 2022 – recalling how tough it is to survive in the EFL with Bolton struggling. For exclusive stories and all the detailed EFL news you need, subscribe to The Football League Paper website, digital edition, or newspaper from as little as 14p a day. Ruthless On his former club Bolton, who sit 19th in the Championship, Fortune told Mr Gamble : “For Bolton and for everyone, the Championship is ruthless. I was with Reading a couple of years ago. You have to go on such an unbelievable run and have such an amazing squad to survive and get out of the Championship. “My goodness, it’s relentless. Like I said, you can win this week, you’re playing three games, you’re flying, boom, you win three games, boom, you’re up the table. “The week after, you lose three games and you sit there thinking: ‘What has happened?’ “Consistency. And it’s not easy. It’s not easy. “But you can congratulate any manager and any team that can get out of the Championship. It’s a huge effort, and you need every single player to be honest, because it’s relentless.” He added: “When you look at the Championship and you look at some of the teams that came down from the Premier League, there are big teams with big players down there “The competition is so high now, and the level of quality in the Championship is just unbelievable.” READ MORE: Millwall handed partial stadium ban following discriminatory chanting The post Quinton Fortune: Championship is ‘relentless’ for Bolton Wanderers appeared first on The League Paper . item.title: Woltemade is giving Juventus’ attack a new dimension
item.description: TURIN, ITALY - NOVEMBER 22: Nick Woltemade of Juventus celebrates after scoring an goal during the Serie A match between Juventus and Venezia FC at Allianz Stadium on November 22, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Alberto Gandolfo - Juventus/Juventus FC via Getty Images) | Juventus FC via Getty Images A 4-0 win in Serie A is difficult to complain about. Juventus were the better team against Venezia on Sunday afternoon, created more and better chances, and eventually turned a competitive first half into a comprehensive victory. The underlying numbers support the result, even if the final margin was somewhat more emphatic than the expected performance would suggest. But the scoreline obscures an interesting distinction between the two halves. Juventus generated just 0.57 expected goals in the 52 minutes the match spent level. After taking the lead, they produced another 1.27 xG in just 41 minutes, scoring three additional goals. Something changed beyond the team’s ability to finish its chances. Juventus became a considerably more functional attacking side. The most obvious explanation is Nick Woltemade’s introduction at halftime. His contribution extended well beyond the goal and assist, however. He changed the way Juventus could progress the ball, connect their midfield and attack, and use the movement of the players around him. In doing so, he also raised an interesting question about how Juve manager Luciano Spalletti should construct his forward line going forward. Spalletti was fairly direct in his assessment of the first half , identifying a lack of movement and poor decision-making in possession as the primary problems: In the first half, we gave the ball away too cheaply, there was nobody moving from their positions, nobody following the flow of the pass, so it was fundamental the players recognised we were missing something, which we provided in the second half. The important part of that assessment is the relationship between movement and possession. Juventus weren’t necessarily struggling because they lacked technically capable players or couldn’t establish territorial control. They struggled because the players around the ball weren’t consistently creating useful options for the player in possession. When teammates remain stationary, passing lanes become predictable, opponents can defend smaller areas, and progression becomes increasingly dependent on individual actions. That was reflected in the first-half chance creation. Juventus managed only six shots and 0.57 xG while the match was level, with Venezia finding opportunities to threaten without producing a particularly dangerous volume of chances themselves. The issue wasn’t simply that Juventus failed to score. They weren’t generating enough threatening situations in the first place. Spalletti’s halftime response addressed that problem, although the improvement also fits into a broader pattern of his game management this season. item.title: ‘It always bites you’: Jeff Saturday says the Cincinnati Bengals need to make a change immediately
item.description: Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images The Cincinnati Bengals suffered a surprising loss at the hands of the Washington Commanders in Week 11, which saw Joe Burrow struggle to have a meaningful impact on the offence. The Bengals were leading until the final minute of the game when Drew Stevens’ 26-yard field goal handed them a rare defeat. Cincinnati only managed 20 points on the night, in large part due to Washington’s defence forcing Burrow to settle for checkdowns all game. On the back of the MVP candidate being neutralised, Jeff Saturday has suggested that the Bengals are too reliant on the passing game, which he thinks ‘always bites you’. In turn, Saturday has suggested that the 7-3 side get back to running the ball more and ‘get back to having balance’. Speaking to ESPN , he said: “They need to get back to having balance. That doesn’t mean you run the ball 40 times a game. I’m not saying you take it out of Joe Burrow’s hands, but you have to be able to beat teams in more than one way. “And at this point, the Bengals keep showing you they want to rely on the passing game, which, by the way, lengthens games and gives teams an opportunity, with 50 seconds or more left in games, to come back and beat you. It always bites you. “I lived in this world for 14 years. I understand great offensive play. We won one Super Bowl, and the year we did, we ran for over 150 yards in every playoff game, or averaged 150 in the playoff games. That matters. I’m just telling you, it matters.” The Bengals’ overreliance on their passing game is glaringly obvious when looking at the stats. They top the NFL for passing yards with 3095 and have the highest completion rate (74.2%). However, when it comes to rushing, they have the second-lowest yards (794), with the Green Bay Packers the only side below them (670). By comparison, other top teams in the NFL clearly have a more balanced approach, which allows them to beat teams in multiple ways. The San Francisco 49ers have 2629 passing yards and 1386 rushing yards, while the Buffalo Bills have 2557 passing yards and 1469 rushing yards. item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.title: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟
item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. In his first full campaign, the Man City-bound starlet emerged as one of the league's most exciting young talents, finishing with with a career-high 23 goal contributions (nine goals, 14 assists) in 29 appearances, and recorded a goal contribution in 10 consecutive matches, the longest such run by a teenager in MLS history. Both his total of 23 goal contributions and his 14 assists are the most ever by a teenager in a single MLS season. Sullivan's form also earned him MLS Player of the Month honors for September 2026. At 17 years and two days old, he became the youngest winner of the award in league history. His production on the club level soon translated to the international stage. Sullivan received his first call-up to the US men's national team in September and made his debut against Peru, becoming the second-youngest player in USMNT history to start a match. He has since collected four senior caps and added another milestone to his résumé by scoring against Mexico at 17 years and five days old, making him the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history.

item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Providing our players with a high-quality surface to compete is a responsibility we take very seriously.” The Gotham FC starting eleven line up before the NWSL playoff quarterfinal in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. The pitch condition was once again a major sticking point after Gotham’s ugly quarterfinal win against the Seattle Reign. Retiring Reign midfielder Jess Fishlock called the field “atrocious.” Gotham defender Jess Carter was overheard saying the grounds were “so bad” when walking through the tunnel after the match. A week after Jaelin Howell injured her right ankle during a home game, the Gotham midfielder said the field was “pretty sandy” and “a little unstable.” Amorós acknowledged the rough conditions impacted the quality of the game. Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
